sections.h2: Who bills property tax in Cape Coral
sections.html:
Cape Coral is inside Lee County, so the Lee County Tax Collector mails and collects your bill, and the Lee County Property Appraiser sets the value and rules on exemptions. The city's part is limited to its own millage rate and its special assessments.

Knowing the split saves phone time. Value, mailing address and exemption questions go to the appraiser's office at 239-533-6100. Payments, receipts and refunds go to the tax collector. A question about one specific levy goes to the authority named on that line of the bill.

sections.h2: The Cape Coral market in brief
sections.html: The city has about 236,264 residents, up 21.8% since the 2020 base, and owners occupy 77.2% of homes. Typical home value is $373,500. With that much growth, many sellers hold older, capped assessments, and the people buying from them start from a reset value.

sections.h2: What the city adds on top of the county
sections.html:
Cape Coral levies its own operating millage. Council kept it at 5.1471 mills in the Fiscal Year 2027 budget approved at the September 24 hearing. A mill is one dollar of tax on every thousand dollars of taxable value, and the city rate is only one line among several authorities on your bill.

The same budget keeps the Fire Service Assessment at 81 percent. Fire and solid waste assessments show up as non-ad valorem charges: flat amounts that don't move with your home's value. The city's budget also sets aside $99.2 million for the Police Department, $91.7 million for Fire, $12.9 million for road repaving and $50.4 million for the municipal charter school system, which is useful if a buyer asks what the city portion pays for.

  • Ad valorem lines: city, county, school board and special districts, each with its own millage.
  • Non-ad valorem lines: city fire and solid waste assessments and similar service charges.
  • Exact figures for your parcel: the city's Property Checkbook tool lists city tax, assessments and fees by address.

Amendment 3 passed and takes effect January 1, 2027, so it does not change a 2026 bill, which is due by March 31, 2027. The Lee County Tax Collector gives that timing. If you are closing soon, ask the collector or your closing agent which tax year's bill your closing date triggers.

Value is fixed on New Year's Day, exemption paperwork closes at the start of March, bills arrive in November, and the final due date falls at the end of the next March.

Lee County calendar of tax events
WhenWhat happens
January 1Date of assessment for all properties
March 1Filing deadline for all exemptions and agricultural classification
July 1Appraiser submits the assessment roll to the Department of Revenue
AugustTRIM notices mailed; 25 days from mailing to petition the Value Adjustment Board
NovemberBills mailed; 4% discount if paid in November
December, January, FebruaryDiscounts of 3%, 2% and 1%
March 31Bill due in full
April 1Unpaid taxes delinquent

An application filed after the March deadline may still be granted, but it counts for the following year.

Lee County offers three ways to spread or postpone a bill: quarterly installments, partial payments and a homestead deferral.

Installment sign-up runs from the start of November through April 30 each year, and your notice must show an estimate above $100. Four payments follow, the first at a 6% discount, then 4.5%, then 3%, then none. Signing up after April 30 means the plan starts with the next year's taxes.

  • Partial payments cover the current year only, allow up to five payments per account, earn no discount, cannot be made online and exclude delinquent taxes.
  • Homestead deferral: the application deadline is March 31, the deferred tax becomes a lien, and fire insurance naming the office as loss payee is required.
  • If you sell mid-plan, the buyer is responsible for the remaining installments that year.

File with the Lee County Property Appraiser by March 1. The house must be your permanent home on New Year's Day. Florida's exemption reaches $50,000 in two layers: $25,000 against every levy, then up to $25,000 more on value above $50,000 for non-school levies.

Save Our Homes holds yearly growth in assessed value to 3 percent or inflation, whichever is smaller. A sale erases the built-up gap, so the next owner's bill can run well above yours. Portability can carry part of the saving to another Florida homestead if you set it up within the three-year window.

To dispute a value, start with the August TRIM notice. The appraiser allows 25 days after mailing for a Value Adjustment Board petition, and an informal conference with the appraiser is open all year. Bring comparable sales and any repair estimates.

sections.h2: When you sell in Cape Coral
sections.html:
At closing, the agent charges or credits each side its share of the year, but the collector's FAQ says the full year's bill goes to the owner of record.

If a bill reaches you after the sale, forward it to the buyer or the closing agent. Ownership changes travel from the clerk to the appraiser, and that can lag. Unpaid prior-year tax is delinquent after April 1 and is paid off at closing like any other lien. Delinquent taxes can't be paid by personal check or eCheck.

The deed carries Florida stamp tax of 70 cents on each $100 of consideration, and every signer shares liability for it. Read the tax lines and prorations on your closing statement, and have the title company explain each one.

Before you list, ask the collector what is owed on the parcel and whether any installment plan is active. Send your title agent the parcel number and any bill that arrives later. Compare the settlement statement against your bill line by line. If you plan to sell to a cash buyer, the same payoff figure applies, though there is no lender waiting on an appraisal or underwriting, so a clear tax record tends to speed things up.

faqs.q: Which number reaches the Cape Coral appraiser?
faqs.a: Dial 239-533-6100 for value, exemption and address questions. Payments and receipts go through the collector's 239-533-6000 line.

faqs.q: What is Cape Coral's city millage rate?
faqs.a: Council kept the operating millage at 5.1471 in the Fiscal Year 2027 budget approved on September 24. Your total bill adds county, school and other authorities, so check your parcel on the tax collector's site.

faqs.q: When are Lee County taxes delinquent?
faqs.a: On April 1, the day after the March 31 deadline. Once a bill is delinquent, the tax collector won't take a personal check or eCheck.

faqs.q: Does the installment plan transfer when I sell?
faqs.a: The buyer picks it up. A new owner continues the plan for that tax year once installments have started, so settle in the contract who owes the remainder.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Cape Coral house with unpaid tax?
faqs.a: Yes. Any balance is cleared at closing from your proceeds, and the Lee County Tax Collector can tell you what is owed so the title company has the figure.
